citations.review_text:
Portal holds up very well even so many years later, and has super smooth performance on my end.
The puzzles involving portals, cubes, balls and turrets are all good brainteasers that I enjoyed.

For the main story only, this game took me about 90 minutes. There are bonus challenge puzzle chambers to do, which I assume brings it up to 2-2.5 hours.

Personally and subjectively, I would recommend this game on a sale rather than for full price. While the content here is pretty great, there is not a whole lot of it. Though I cannot deny the cultural impact that Portal has made over the years (Including Portal 2).

Portal.

Even though at the time I write this, it is my first time playing, this is a WONDERFUL game. The game runs very smoothly despite my non-gaming computer. While the game is almost 20 years old, it is still fun, and doesn't look as old as it is.

Proper review.
This game is a fun game which makes you think on how to complete the tasks. I have a fun time playing this, while also having a good think of everything. Throughout the game, I was given more tools and more challenges gradually, it carries you one step at a time, teaching you how to complete the levels. Through challenges which made me think for minutes, to challenges where I could complete it easily, it was very enjoyable.

In the game where I could obtain portal guns and make portals to solve the puzzles to get to the next level, I have not regret buying this a single bit.
So, if you are thinking to buy it... buy it! It is definetly worth buying the game!!!

citations.review_text: Crazy good game. Valve really cooked with this one. The physics, ragdoll, Glados were great, advanced maps too. But challenges sucked ass

[h2]Unnecessarily Complicated Portal Review[/h2]

[b]TL;DR:[/b] Portal has a lot more content than I always thought: bonus maps, challenges, and achievements. This is a must-buy for people who like puzzle games. Overall Score: 72/100 - Recommended.

[h3]Unnecessarily Long Version with 5 Categories.[/h3]

[b]Cost per Hour:[/b] $10 for ~7.8 hours of gameplay ($1.28/h). My playtime includes the main game, bonus maps, and all of the challenges. The game often goes on 80-90% sale, so if you, somehow, still don’t own this game, just buy it on sale and give it a try. Category Score: 8/10

[b]Gameplay:[/b] The game is short and not very hard... The main game, that is. Bonus maps and challenges are great ways to prolong the game, but the [spoiler]“Steps”[/spoiler] challenge sucks a lot, I HATE IT! THE ONE RESPONSIBLE FOR IT SHOULD… get a cookie, so they won’t do it ever again. Achievements are mostly fine, except some of the more grindy ones. Category Score: 7/10

[b]Visuals:[/b] This game [i]does[/i] look a little dated, but it never stopped me from enjoying it. That said, I can see how it can be a problem for people who prefer better graphics. Especially the lighting: the game looks very flat, in my opinion. Category Score: 5/10

[b]Sound design:[/b] The sound department is a bit lacking, in my opinion, but nothing bad: the voice acting is good, the sounds that [b][i]are[/i][/b] there are fine, and the radio music is an absolute banger! Category Score: 6/10

[b]Technical performance / Compatibility:[/b] Being developed by Valve, this game has a native Linux version and should work fine on most modern distributions. Couldn’t find any compatibility or performance issues. If the native version doesn’t work, the Proton version should. Category Score: 10/10

single_points.text: One reviewer says the physics are the most agonizing part of the game because they are janky, causing cubes entering portals to jump straight into the liquid.

citation.review_text:
Hi, Portal fan here and i'm here to say- this game is very great!
Aside from their great succesor- the second part, the first part is a very good beggining. i always loved how Valve games started as an concept only to grow bigger in the second game.
I never liked puzzle games that much, but obviously portal differs from any other puzzle games a lot with it's Lore and gameplay.
The ending song shocked me a lot, then it made me smile while i was reading the lyrics..And that's when i really liked GLaDOS' character so much as well as her personality and dark humor. but the flaws? i don't know if it's obivous one but i do have ONE flaw that made me triggered- THE PHYSICS..Good grief, the physics are the most agonizing part of this game!!! it's so janky, everytime i entered the portal with a cube it jumped off the platform and straight into the steel water (or whatever liquid is it) ;-;
but do i recommend this game? well, kinda..Obviously not everyone likes such puzzle games, but if you want to give it a chance, go for it, portal indeed is very different than any other puzzle games you will see.

single_points.text: One reviewer notes that there is a feature to import custom map levels but without Steam Workshop support, making it not popular enough to be viable.

citation.review_text:
+ The combination of an amazing story, physics-based puzzles, and graphics is just perfect. Even after the story, there are harder levels, different challenges, and milestone targets.

- The story took me only around 5 hours for me to beat, without any guides nor prior knowledge, while exploring everything (aka no rush). Meanwhile the extra content is not as encouraging as the storyline. There is the feature to import custom map levels but without Steam Workshop support, and how greatly overshadowed it is by its sequel (Portal 2), it is not popular enough to be viable.

! Context: Portal was one of those games that was sitting in my library, for years untouched, until a friend gifted me Portal 2 (for my birthday :D) which made me start playing Portal after confirming that both games' storylines were in canonical order.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game is short, with playthroughs lasting around three hours.

citations.review_text:
[quote=GLaDOS] [i]Well done, android. The Enrichment Center once again reminds you that android hell is a real place where you will be sent at the first sign of defiance.[/i] [/quote]

I received [i]Portal[/i] for free when I created my Steam account 15 years ago, but I never bothered to experience it al the way thought until now. I was very surprised by how short it was! My playthrough clocked in at around three hours. In many ways it feels more like a tech demo than a full-fledged game, although I admit I am experiencing [i]Portal[/i] far outside the context of its original release, back when it was packaged within "The Orange Box" in 2007 as a brand-new, experimental title.

After nearly two decades of memes and praise, I think anyone with the internet could surmise that the portal gun mechanics and the dialogue by Ellen McLain are the highlights of the game, I'm not sure what more I could say that hasn't already been said. In my first playthrough, I found solving the puzzles exciting and satisfying albeit the narrative elements were lacking — I have to assume that so much of the lore that I have been exposed to on the internet must come from [i]Portal 2[/i].

Not content with ending my playtime after three hours, I went on to chase the achievements which revealed the rough edges of the game to me. "Transmission Received" required a second playthrough but was fun and the radios felt like additional junior puzzles to complete, while the six advanced maps required for "Vanilla Crazy Cake" were harder than the base maps but still satisfying to solve. The challenge maps, however, are not great — the only way to earn the gold medals is to find these weird maneuvers and skips that don't feel like intended game design, and the "steps taken" challenges are ridiculous as the counting feels wildly inconsistent.

In my opinion, while a genuinely fun puzzle game and time-waster, [i]Portal[/i] is probably best played as a prelude to [i]Portal 2[/i], which seems to be a more c…

Portal first arrived in 2007 as part of The Orange Box and turned out to be the surprise star of the bundle. The idea is simple, you hold a gun that creates two linked portals and you use it to get through a series of test chambers. Soon you’re flinging yourself across rooms, using momentum to reach far off ledges and thinking about space in ways no other game had asked you to before.

What makes it work is how well it teaches you. There are no long tutorials. Each chamber introduces one idea, lets you practice it, then quietly builds on it. By the end you’re pulling off moves that would have seemed impossible at the start and it feels like you figured it all out yourself.

GLaDOS is the heart of the game. The calm, passive aggressive AI guiding you through the tests starts out as a slightly odd narrator and slowly becomes something much more sinister and hilarious. Her dark humor, along with the Weighted Companion Cube and the famous promise of cake made Portal one of the most quoted games of its era. The way the story unfolds through her voice and the hidden rooms behind the walls is subtle and memorable.

It’s also a short game, usually two to four hours and that works in its favor. There’s no filler and every chamber feels purposeful. The ending, capped off by one of the best credits songs in gaming is a perfect send off.

Portal is a compact masterpiece. It’s smart, funny. tightly designed and its influence can still be felt in puzzle games today ultimately serving as a great proof of concept for its sequel Portal 2 which builds on it perfectly. If you haven’t played Portal it’s well worth a few hours of your time.

A short but effective little game. Made to be a pack-in game for The Orange Box, it's not really meant to stand on its own as a full experience, but somehow it kind of does anyways. The optional challenge content is really satisfying to complete, and the puzzles can be very confusing your first time playing a Portal game. I think everyone should play through this ~3 hour game at least once.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the least steps challenges are poorly designed and frustrating, citing issues with visibility and inconsistent counters.

citations.review_text: Love this game but whoever designed the least steps challenges needs to be fired

The absolute gold standard for a brief game. Aesthetics? On point. Timeless. Stunning. Puzzles? A little on the easy side, but if you want a challenge there's always the Bonus Maps. Writing? Wonderful. Fun. A true companion. Music? "Still Alive" has been stuck in my head for weeks.
But those achievements?
WHO thought "least steps" was a good idea??? Did they find work at Arkane a few years later and put together Dunwall City Trials?? One of the worst challenges I've ever been put through.

PC Gaming Through the Years: A Survey - #19 (2007)

listen it's a great game. it's short and honestly if we're talking about gameplay feel, mechanics, content and length then portal 2 is what you'll love. BUT portal 1 is still an amazing game and to get a feel for portal mechanics u should play this game first and also cuz portal 2 is a sequel so... yeah story wise play this one first

besides that there are things that stop it from being a 10/10. first off there are challenge maps for the last 6 chambers in the game. there are 3 challenges being least portals, least time and least steps. let me tell u this now DO NOT DO THEM. least portals are fun but that's about it. time is okayish but it does need u being fast and sometimes it's unfair even if doable. but the steps one is actual brain cancer. there's really only one chamber thats easy with all 3 but it requires u knowing portal bumping so... without it and knowing where to use it on the specific chamber ur screwed. 

besides that there's a new game + achievement where after u beat the game radios will show up in every test chamber and have a light, even the ones that showed up in new game have a light. but it's new game + only so dont worry too much. besides from that there's camera shy which u need to detach every camera that's detachable from the wall in one playthrough but can be done on new game (it tracks save unlike radios where it counts no matter what). there achievable but do require u to replay through the game (assuming u didn't do the camera one on first playthrough) so it's up to u

besides that tho the games fun and i recommend u buy it on sale!
who ever came up with the least steps challenges deserves to rot in the lowest level of hell imaginable

the concept of the game is very nice. However, the execution was horrible. Completing the main story and the advanced maps are fine but the challenges are quite annoying. The portal mechanics in this game are horrible and disorientating. Sometimes, when you exit a portal, you can spin and maneuver. Other times, you are caught in this position where you cant aim and maneuver. The steps challenges are horribly designed because you cant see your own feet. So you dont know how many steps youre really taking and now have to rely on this counter {which is very inconsistent and finnicky) to tell you how many steps you are taking. The concept is very nice and I see why this game is very popular. However, the devs did a horrible job executing this - even for devs that made this in 2007. The game is very small and linear so there shouldn't be an excuse of lazy and haphazard development. Completing the challenges does require skill but a lot of luck is required too. And that... I cannot forgive.

citations.review_text:
Interesting game with problem solving at the core. Overall I WOULD recommend the game. Fun little weekend getaway. But just a few nitpicks:
- Did drag a bit at the end (even for a short game)
- The red screens when dying made my eyes bleed.
- Felt a little nauseous when portalling into loops.
But if you want some logic/puzzlie type things it's worth it!
